newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RANGERS SIGN WORLD SERIES MVP WETTELAND FOR FOUR YEARS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RANGERS SIGN WORLD SERIES MVP WETTELAND FOR FOUR YEARS.

text.p: The Texas Rangers signed All-Star closing pitcher John Wetteland to a four-year contract worth $23 million on Monday.

Wetteland, a 30-year-old right-hander, became the first pitcher to save all four games in a World Series. He also was the first reliever to win World Series MVP honours since Oakland's Rollie Fingers in 1974.
The Yankees won four straight games after losing the first two games to Atlanta in the 1996 World Series.

Wetteland combined with Panamanian Mariano Rivera to give New York the best bullpen tandem in baseball. Wetteland was 2-3 with a 2.82 ERA in 62 relief appearances, converting 43 of 46 save opportunities.
The loss of Wetteland moves Rivera into the role of closer for the Yankees.
Wetteland is expected to fill a glaring need for the Rangers, who lost inconsistent closer Mike Henneman to free agency. Henneman was 0-7 with 31 saves and a 5.79 ERA.
